title: Derived represented functor comparison normalized on resolution cocycles
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category with morphisms in universe $v$, with injective resolutions [def-sp-injective-resolutions] and $\operatorname{HasExt}^{v}$. Let $A\in\mathcal A$, let $H:\mathcal A\to\mathrm{Ab}^{v}$ be additive, and let $e:\operatorname{Hom}(A,-)\simeq H$ be an additive natural isomorphism. There exist natural isomorphisms $x_n:R^nH\simeq\operatorname{Ext}^n(A,-)$ for every $n\ge0$, normalized as follows. For every $Y$, every injective resolution $I$ of $Y$, every cocycle $s:A\to I^p$, and every $c\in Z^p(H(I))$ whose image under the cycle inclusion is $e_{I^p}(s)$, one has $\rho_I(x_p(Y)^{-1}(I.\mathrm{extMk}(s)))=\pi(c)$. Here $\rho_I$ is the canonical right-derived resolution comparison [lem-sp-derived-well-defined] and $\pi:Z^p(H(I))\to H^p(H(I))$ is the homology projection. There is no second category, pushforward, or augmented comparison in this statement.

proof.text: For each chosen injective resolution, use Mathlib InjectiveResolution.extAddEquivCohomologyClass and HomComplex.leftHomologyData to identify Ext with homology of the Hom complex. Cochain.fromSingleEquiv identifies this complex with additive Hom applied to the resolution. Its differential formula Cochain.δ_fromSingleMk proves compatibility. Apply e degreewise and compose the resulting homology isomorphism with the canonical right-derived resolution comparison. This gives the inverse components of x.

A lift of a coefficient map acts by postcomposition on Hom complexes. The from-single identification and e commute with postcomposition. InjectiveResolution.extMk_comp_mk₀ computes the Ext map on cocycles, and isoRightDerivedObj_hom_naturality computes the derived map, proving naturality. A comparison lifting the identity transfers this construction to any other resolution, independently of the lift up to homotopy.

InjectiveResolution.extEquivCohomologyClass_extMk identifies extMk(s) with its from-single cocycle class. Under the degreewise identifications the underlying cycle is e(s). The hypothesis iCycles(c)=e(s) and monicity of iCycles identify this cycle with c. Its class is homologyπ(c), proving the normalization.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_ext_rightDerived_cocycle_comparison
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C] [HasExt.{v} C]
    [HasInjectiveResolutions C] (A : C) (H : C ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{v}) [H.Additive]
    (e : preadditiveCoyoneda.obj (op A) ≅ H) :
    ∃ x : ∀ n : ℕ, H.rightDerived n ≅ (Abelian.extFunctor n).obj (op A),
      ∀ (Y : C) (I : InjectiveResolution Y) (p : ℕ)
        (s : A ⟶ I.cocomplex.X p) (hs : s ≫ I.cocomplex.d p (p + 1) = 0)
        (c : ((H.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj I.cocomplex).cycles p)
        (hc : ((H.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj I.cocomplex).iCycles p c =
          e.hom.app (I.cocomplex.X p) s),
        (I.isoRightDerivedObj H p).hom ((x p).inv.app Y (I.extMk s (p + 1) rfl hs)) =
          ((H.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj I.cocomplex).homologyπ p c
